-- ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
local ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("lsp_hierarchy_hl")

---@type table<integer, {[1]: string, [2]: string}>
local KIND_ICONS = {
  [1]  = { "󰈔 ", "Structure" },            -- File
  [2]  = { "󰆧 ", "Structure" },            -- Module
  [3]  = { "󰅪 ", "Structure" },            -- Namespace
  [4]  = { "󰏗 ", "Structure" },            -- Package
  [5]  = { " ", "@lsp.type.class" },       -- Class
  [6]  = { " ", "@lsp.type.method" },      -- Method
  [7]  = { " ", "Identifier" },            -- Property
  [8]  = { "󰜢 ", "Identifier" },            -- Field
  [9]  = { " ", "@constructor" },          -- Constructor
  [10] = { " ", "@lsp.type.enum" },        -- Enum
  [11] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Interface
  [12] = { "󰊕 ", "Function" },              -- Function
  [13] = { " ", "@variable" },             -- Variable
  [14] = { "󰏿 ", "@constant" },             -- Constant
  [15] = { " ", "String" },                -- String
  [16] = { "󰎠 ", "Number" },                -- Number
  [17] = { "◩ ", "Boolean" },               -- Boolean
  [18] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Array
  [19] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Object
  [20] = { "󰌋 ", "Identifier" },            -- Key
  [21] = { "󰟢 ", "Comment" },               -- Null
  [22] = { " ", "@lsp.type.enumMember" },  -- EnumMember
  [23] = { "󰙅 ", "Structure" },             -- Struct
  [24] = { " ", "Special" },               -- Event
  [25] = { "󰆕 ", "Operator" },              -- Operator
  [26] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- TypeParameter
}
local KIND_FALLBACK = { "? ", "NonText" }

local GUIDE_MID    = "├─ "
local GUIDE_LAST   = "└─ "
local GUIDE_NESTED = "│  "
local GUIDE_SPACE  = "   "

-- ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function get_short_path(uri)
  local path = vim.uri_to_fname(uri)
  local cwd = vim.fn.getcwd() .. "/"
  if path:sub(1, #cwd) == cwd then
    path = path:sub(#cwd + 1)
  end
  return path
end

local function make_node(item, from_ranges, depth)
  local range = item.selectionRange or item.range
  return {
    name = item.name,
    detail = item.detail or "",
    kind = item.kind,
    uri = item.uri,
    range = range,
    from_ranges = from_ranges,
    children = {},
    expanded = false,
    depth = depth or 0,
    -- Keep the original item for subsequent LSP requests
    _item = item,
  }
end

-- ── Tree rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

--- Renders the tree into lines with extmark highlight data.
---@param nodes table[]
---@param lines string[]
---@param line_map table[]
---@param extmarks table[][] array of {col_start, col_end, hl_group} per line
---@param last_flags table<integer, boolean> tracks which ancestor depths were last-child
local function render_tree(nodes, lines, line_map, extmarks, last_flags)
  last_flags = last_flags or {}
  lines = lines or {}
  line_map = line_map or {}
  extmarks = extmarks or {}

  for i, node in ipairs(nodes) do
    local depth = node.depth
    local is_last = (i == #nodes)
    local line_extmarks = {}
    local col = 0

    -- Build guide prefix for ancestor levels
    local prefix = ""
    for d = 1, depth - 1 do
      local guide = last_flags[d] and GUIDE_SPACE or GUIDE_NESTED
      prefix = prefix .. guide
    end

    -- Connector (root nodes have none)
    local connector = ""
    if depth > 0 then
      connector = is_last and GUIDE_LAST or GUIDE_MID
    end

    local guide_str = prefix .. connector
    if #guide_str > 0 then
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #guide_str, "NonText" })
      col = col + #guide_str
    end

    local line

    if node._loading then
      -- Synthetic loading placeholder
      local text = "⟳ loading..."
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #text, "Comment" })
      line = guide_str .. text

    elseif node._error then
      -- Synthetic error placeholder
      local text = "✗ " .. (node._error_msg or "error resolving calls")
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #text, "DiagnosticError" })
      line = guide_str .. text

    else
      -- Toggle icon
      local toggle_icon
      if #node.children > 0 or not node._resolved then
        toggle_icon = node.expanded and "▼ " or "► "
      else
        toggle_icon = "· "
      end
      local toggle_hl = toggle_icon == "· " and "NonText" or "Special"
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #toggle_icon, toggle_hl })
      col = col + #toggle_icon

      -- Kind icon
      local kind_entry = KIND_ICONS[node.kind] or KIND_FALLBACK
      local kind_str = kind_entry[1]
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #kind_str, kind_entry[2] })
      col = col + #kind_str

      -- Function name
      local name_str = node.name .. "()"
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #name_str, "Function" })
      col = col + #name_str

      -- Location
      local location = ""
      if node.uri then
        local path = get_short_path(node.uri)
        local lnum = node.range and (node.range.start.line + 1) or ""
        location = string.format(" [%s:%s]", path, lnum)
        table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #location, "Comment" })
      end

      line = guide_str .. toggle_icon .. kind_str .. name_str .. location
    end

    table.insert(lines, line)
    table.insert(line_map, node)
    table.insert(extmarks, line_extmarks)

    -- Recurse into expanded children
    if node.expanded and #node.children > 0 then
      local old = last_flags[depth]
      last_flags[depth] = is_last
      render_tree(node.children, lines, line_map, extmarks, last_flags)
      last_flags[depth] = old
    end
  end

  return lines, line_map, extmarks
end

-- ── Buffer management ────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
  local lines, line_map, ext = render_tree(root_nodes)
  state.line_map = line_map

  local ok, cursor = pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor, 0)
  if not ok then cursor = { 1, 0 } end

  vim.bo[buf].modifiable = true
  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, lines)
  vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false

  -- Apply extmark highlights
  vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, ns, 0, -1)
  for line_idx, line_ext in ipairs(ext) do
    for _, e in ipairs(line_ext) do
      pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark, buf, ns, line_idx - 1, e[1], {
        end_col = e[2],
        hl_group = e[3],
      })
    end
  end

  -- Restore cursor
  local max_line = #lines
  if cursor[1] > max_line then
    cursor[1] = max_line
  end
  if max_line > 0 then
    pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, 0, cursor)
  end
end

-- ── LSP resolution ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function resolve_children(client, node, direction, bufnr, callback)
  local method = direction == "incoming"
    and "callHierarchy/incomingCalls"
    or "callHierarchy/outgoingCalls"

  local item = node._item
  client:request(method, { item = item }, function(err, result)
    if err then
      callback(nil, err)
      return
    end
    if not result then
      callback({})
      return
    end

    local children = {}
    for _, call in ipairs(result) do
      local source = direction == "incoming" and call.from or call.to
      local from_ranges = call.fromRanges
      local child = make_node(source, from_ranges, node.depth + 1)
      table.insert(children, child)
    end
    callback(children)
  end, bufnr)
end

--- Recursively resolves children up to max_depth levels using async fan-out.
local function resolve_to_depth(client, node, direction, bufnr, max_depth, callback)
  if node.depth >= max_depth then
    callback()
    return
  end

  resolve_children(client, node, direction, bufnr, function(children, err)
    if err or not children then
      node.children = {}
      node._resolved = true
      callback()
      return
    end

    node.children = children
    node._resolved = true
    node.expanded = true

    -- Count children that need further resolution
    local pending = 0
    for _, child in ipairs(children) do
      child._resolved = false
      if node.depth + 1 < max_depth then
        pending = pending + 1
      end
    end

    if pending == 0 then
      callback()
      return
    end

    local completed = 0
    for _, child in ipairs(children) do
      if node.depth + 1 < max_depth then
        resolve_to_depth(client, child, direction, bufnr, max_depth, function()
          completed = completed + 1
          if completed == pending then
            callback()
          end
        end)
      end
    end
  end)
end

-- ── Main entry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function M.show(direction, opts)
  direction = direction or "incoming"
  opts = opts or {}
  local max_depth = opts.depth or 2

  local source_buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
  local source_win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
  local params = vim.lsp.util.make_position_params(0, "utf-16")

  local clients = vim.lsp.get_clients({
    bufnr = source_buf,
    method = "textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy",
  })

  if #clients == 0 then
    vim.notify("No LSP client supports call hierarchy", vim.log.levels.WARN)
    return
  end

  local client = clients[1]

  client:request("textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy", params, function(err, result)
    if err or not result or #result == 0 then
      vim.notify("No call hierarchy item found at cursor", vim.log.levels.WARN)
      return
    end

    vim.schedule(function()
      local root_item = result[1]
      local root_node = make_node(root_item, nil, 0)
      root_node.expanded = true

      local buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
      vim.bo[buf].buftype = "nofile"
      vim.bo[buf].bufhidden = "wipe"
      vim.bo[buf].filetype = "lsp-hierarchy"
      vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false

      local title = direction == "incoming" and "Incoming Calls" or "Outgoing Calls"
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_name(buf, string.format("[%s] %s()", title, root_node.name))

      local state = { line_map = {} }
      local root_nodes = { root_node }

      -- Resolve to configured depth, then display
      resolve_to_depth(client, root_node, direction, source_buf, max_depth, function()
        vim.schedule(function()
          refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)

          -- Open in a horizontal split at bottom
          vim.cmd("botright vsplit")
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(0, buf)
          vim.cmd("wincmd J")
          vim.cmd("resize 15")
          vim.wo.number = false
          vim.wo.relativenumber = false
          vim.wo.signcolumn = "no"
          vim.wo.cursorline = true
          vim.wo.wrap = false

          -- Auto-preview: show call site in source window on cursor move
          vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("CursorMoved", {
            buffer = buf,
            callback = function()
              if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then return end
              local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
              local node = state.line_map[lnum]
              if not node or not node.uri or node._loading or node._error then return end

              pcall(function()
                local target_buf = vim.uri_to_bufnr(node.uri)
                vim.fn.bufload(target_buf)
                vim.api.nvim_win_call(source_win, function()
                  vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(source_win, target_buf)
                  if node.range then
                    vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(source_win, {
                      node.range.start.line + 1,
                      node.range.start.character,
                    })
                    vim.cmd("normal! zz")
                  end
                end)
              end)
            end,
          })

          -- Jump to definition (focuses source window)
          local function jump()
            local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
            local node = state.line_map[lnum]
            if not node or not node.uri then return end

            if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then return end

            local target_buf = vim.uri_to_bufnr(node.uri)
            vim.fn.bufload(target_buf)
            vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(source_win)
            vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(source_win, target_buf)
            if node.range then
              vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(source_win, {
                node.range.start.line + 1,
                node.range.start.character,
              })
              vim.cmd("normal! zz")
            end
          end

          -- Toggle expand/collapse
          local function toggle()
            local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
            local node = state.line_map[lnum]
            if not node or node._loading or node._error then return end

            if node.expanded then
              node.expanded = false
              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
            elseif node._resolved then
              node.expanded = true
              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
            else
              -- Show loading indicator immediately
              node.children = { {
                _loading = true,
                name = "loading...",
                depth = node.depth + 1,
                children = {},
              } }
              node.expanded = true
              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)

              -- Resolve children asynchronously
              resolve_children(client, node, direction, source_buf, function(children, resolve_err)
                vim.schedule(function()
                  if resolve_err then
                    node.children = { {
                      _error = true,
                      _error_msg = tostring(resolve_err),
                      name = "error",
                      depth = node.depth + 1,
                      children = {},
                    } }
                  else
                    node.children = children or {}
                    for _, child in ipairs(node.children) do
                      child._resolved = false
                    end
                  end
                  node._resolved = true
                  refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
                end)
              end)
            end
          end

          local bopts = { buffer = buf, nowait = true, silent = true }
          vim.keymap.set("n", "<CR>", jump, bopts)
          vim.keymap.set("n", "o", toggle, bopts)
          vim.keymap.set("n", "q", "<cmd>close<cr>", bopts)
          vim.keymap.set("n", "<Esc>", "<cmd>close<cr>", bopts)
        end)
      end)
    end)
  end, source_buf)
end

function M.incoming(opts) M.show("incoming", opts) end
function M.outgoing(opts) M.show("outgoing", opts) end

return M

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **LSP offset encoding is a common pitfall**: LSP `character` fields use the negotiated encoding (usually UTF-16), not byte offsets. Using them raw in `nvim_win_set_cursor` causes wrong column placement on lines with multibyte text. `_get_line_byte_from_position` handles the conversion.
- **Per-node generation counters** are better than a global counter for staleness — expanding node A shouldn't invalidate the in-flight resolve for node B.
- **`from_ranges`** is the most actionable data in call hierarchy responses — it points to *where the call happens* rather than where the function is defined, which is what users actually want to see when navigating a call chain.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

-- LSP Call Hierarchy Tree Viewer
--
-- Displays incoming or outgoing call chains as an interactive tree.
-- Equivalent to telescope-hierarchy.nvim but works without telescope.
--
-- Usage:
--   :LspIncomingCallsTree [depth]  - Show who calls the function under cursor
--   :LspOutgoingCallsTree [depth]  - Show what the function under cursor calls
--
-- Buffer keymaps:
--   <CR>  Jump to call site (in source window)
--   o     Toggle expand/collapse node
--   q     Close the hierarchy buffer

local M = {}

-- ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
local ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("lsp_hierarchy_hl")

---@type table<integer, {[1]: string, [2]: string}>
local KIND_ICONS = {
  [1]  = { "󰈔 ", "Structure" },            -- File
  [2]  = { "󰆧 ", "Structure" },            -- Module
  [3]  = { "󰅪 ", "Structure" },            -- Namespace
  [4]  = { "󰏗 ", "Structure" },            -- Package
  [5]  = { " ", "@lsp.type.class" },       -- Class
  [6]  = { " ", "@lsp.type.method" },      -- Method
  [7]  = { " ", "Identifier" },            -- Property
  [8]  = { "󰜢 ", "Identifier" },            -- Field
  [9]  = { " ", "@constructor" },          -- Constructor
  [10] = { " ", "@lsp.type.enum" },        -- Enum
  [11] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Interface
  [12] = { "󰊕 ", "Function" },              -- Function
  [13] = { " ", "@variable" },             -- Variable
  [14] = { "󰏿 ", "@constant" },             -- Constant
  [15] = { " ", "String" },                -- String
  [16] = { "󰎠 ", "Number" },                -- Number
  [17] = { "◩ ", "Boolean" },               -- Boolean
  [18] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Array
  [19] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Object
  [20] = { "󰌋 ", "Identifier" },            -- Key
  [21] = { "󰟢 ", "Comment" },               -- Null
  [22] = { " ", "@lsp.type.enumMember" },  -- EnumMember
  [23] = { "󰙅 ", "Structure" },             -- Struct
  [24] = { " ", "Special" },               -- Event
  [25] = { "󰆕 ", "Operator" },              -- Operator
  [26] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- TypeParameter
}
local KIND_FALLBACK = { "? ", "NonText" }

local GUIDE_MID    = "├─ "
local GUIDE_LAST   = "└─ "
local GUIDE_NESTED = "│  "
local GUIDE_SPACE  = "   "

-- ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function get_short_path(uri)
  local path = vim.uri_to_fname(uri)
  local cwd = vim.fn.getcwd() .. "/"
  if path:sub(1, #cwd) == cwd then
    path = path:sub(#cwd + 1)
  end
  return path
end

--- Returns the best navigation position for a node: call site (from_ranges)
--- first, falling back to the symbol's selection/definition range.
local function get_nav_position(node)
  if node.from_ranges and node.from_ranges[1] then
    return node.from_ranges[1].start
  end
  if node.range then
    return node.range.start
  end
  return nil
end

--- Converts an LSP position to a Neovim cursor tuple {1-indexed line, byte col},
--- respecting the client's offset encoding (utf-8/utf-16/utf-32).
local function lsp_pos_to_cursor(target_buf, pos, offset_encoding)
  local row = pos.line + 1
  if pos.character == 0 then
    return { row, 0 }
  end
  -- _get_line_byte_from_position handles encoding conversion internally
  local ok, byte_col = pcall(
    vim.lsp.util._get_line_byte_from_position,
    target_buf, pos, offset_encoding
  )
  if ok then
    return { row, byte_col }
  end
  return { row, pos.character }
end

local function make_node(item, from_ranges, depth)
  local range = item.selectionRange or item.range
  return {
    name = item.name,
    detail = item.detail or "",
    kind = item.kind,
    uri = item.uri,
    range = range,
    from_ranges = from_ranges,
    children = {},
    expanded = false,
    depth = depth or 0,
    -- Keep the original item for subsequent LSP requests
    _item = item,
  }
end

-- ── Tree rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

--- Renders the tree into lines with extmark highlight data.
---@param nodes table[]
---@param lines string[]
---@param line_map table[]
---@param extmarks table[][] array of {col_start, col_end, hl_group} per line
---@param last_flags table<integer, boolean> tracks which ancestor depths were last-child
local function render_tree(nodes, lines, line_map, extmarks, last_flags)
  last_flags = last_flags or {}
  lines = lines or {}
  line_map = line_map or {}
  extmarks = extmarks or {}

  for i, node in ipairs(nodes) do
    local depth = node.depth
    local is_last = (i == #nodes)
    local line_extmarks = {}
    local col = 0

    -- Build guide prefix for ancestor levels
    local prefix = ""
    for d = 1, depth - 1 do
      local guide = last_flags[d] and GUIDE_SPACE or GUIDE_NESTED
      prefix = prefix .. guide
    end

    -- Connector (root nodes have none)
    local connector = ""
    if depth > 0 then
      connector = is_last and GUIDE_LAST or GUIDE_MID
    end

    local guide_str = prefix .. connector
    if #guide_str > 0 then
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #guide_str, "NonText" })
      col = col + #guide_str
    end

    local line

    if node._loading then
      -- Synthetic loading placeholder
      local text = "⟳ loading..."
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #text, "Comment" })
      line = guide_str .. text

    elseif node._error then
      -- Synthetic error placeholder
      local text = "✗ " .. (node._error_msg or "error resolving calls")
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #text, "DiagnosticError" })
      line = guide_str .. text

    else
      -- Toggle icon
      local toggle_icon
      if #node.children > 0 or not node._resolved then
        toggle_icon = node.expanded and "▼ " or "► "
      else
        toggle_icon = "· "
      end
      local toggle_hl = toggle_icon == "· " and "NonText" or "Special"
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #toggle_icon, toggle_hl })
      col = col + #toggle_icon

      -- Kind icon
      local kind_entry = KIND_ICONS[node.kind] or KIND_FALLBACK
      local kind_str = kind_entry[1]
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #kind_str, kind_entry[2] })
      col = col + #kind_str

      -- Function name
      local name_str = node.name .. "()"
      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #name_str, "Function" })
      col = col + #name_str

      -- Location: show call site line (from_ranges) when available
      local location = ""
      if node.uri then
        local path = get_short_path(node.uri)
        local nav_pos = get_nav_position(node)
        local lnum = nav_pos and (nav_pos.line + 1) or ""
        location = string.format(" [%s:%s]", path, lnum)
        table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #location, "Comment" })
      end

      line = guide_str .. toggle_icon .. kind_str .. name_str .. location
    end

    table.insert(lines, line)
    table.insert(line_map, node)
    table.insert(extmarks, line_extmarks)

    -- Recurse into expanded children
    if node.expanded and #node.children > 0 then
      local old = last_flags[depth]
      last_flags[depth] = is_last
      render_tree(node.children, lines, line_map, extmarks, last_flags)
      last_flags[depth] = old
    end
  end

  return lines, line_map, extmarks
end

-- ── Buffer management ────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
  if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) then return end

  local lines, line_map, ext = render_tree(root_nodes)
  state.line_map = line_map

  -- Save cursor from the hierarchy window (not window 0)
  local win = state.hier_win
  local cursor = { 1, 0 }
  if win and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(win) then
    local ok, pos = pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor, win)
    if ok then cursor = pos end
  end

  vim.bo[buf].modifiable = true
  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, lines)
  vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false

  -- Apply extmark highlights
  vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, ns, 0, -1)
  for line_idx, line_ext in ipairs(ext) do
    for _, e in ipairs(line_ext) do
      pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark, buf, ns, line_idx - 1, e[1], {
        end_col = e[2],
        hl_group = e[3],
      })
    end
  end

  -- Restore cursor in the hierarchy window only
  local max_line = #lines
  if cursor[1] > max_line then
    cursor[1] = max_line
  end
  if max_line > 0 and win and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(win) then
    pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, win, cursor)
  end
end

-- ── LSP resolution ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
local function resolve_children(client, node, direction, bufnr, callback)
  local method = direction == "incoming"
    and "callHierarchy/incomingCalls"
    or "callHierarchy/outgoingCalls"

  local item = node._item
  client:request(method, { item = item }, function(err, result)
    if err then
      callback(nil, err)
      return
    end
    if not result then
      callback({})
      return
    end

    local children = {}
    for _, call in ipairs(result) do
      local source = direction == "incoming" and call.from or call.to
      local from_ranges = call.fromRanges
      local child = make_node(source, from_ranges, node.depth + 1)
      table.insert(children, child)
    end
    callback(children)
  end, bufnr)
end

--- Recursively resolves children up to max_depth levels using async fan-out.
local function resolve_to_depth(client, node, direction, bufnr, max_depth, callback)
  if node.depth >= max_depth then
    callback()
    return
  end

  resolve_children(client, node, direction, bufnr, function(children, err)
    if err or not children then
      node.children = {}
      node._resolved = true
      callback()
      return
    end

    node.children = children
    node._resolved = true
    node.expanded = true

    -- Count children that need further resolution
    local pending = 0
    for _, child in ipairs(children) do
      child._resolved = false
      if node.depth + 1 < max_depth then
        pending = pending + 1
      end
    end

    if pending == 0 then
      callback()
      return
    end

    local completed = 0
    for _, child in ipairs(children) do
      if node.depth + 1 < max_depth then
        resolve_to_depth(client, child, direction, bufnr, max_depth, function()
          completed = completed + 1
          if completed == pending then
            callback()
          end
        end)
      end
    end
  end)
end

-- ── Main entry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function M.show(direction, opts)
  direction = direction or "incoming"
  opts = opts or {}
  local max_depth = opts.depth or 2

  local source_buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
  local source_win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
  local params = vim.lsp.util.make_position_params(0, "utf-16")

  local clients = vim.lsp.get_clients({
    bufnr = source_buf,
    method = "textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy",
  })

  if #clients == 0 then
    vim.notify("No LSP client supports call hierarchy", vim.log.levels.WARN)
    return
  end

  local client = clients[1]
  local offset_encoding = client.offset_encoding or "utf-16"

  client:request("textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy", params, function(err, result)
    if err or not result or #result == 0 then
      vim.notify("No call hierarchy item found at cursor", vim.log.levels.WARN)
      return
    end

    vim.schedule(function()
      local root_item = result[1]
      local root_node = make_node(root_item, nil, 0)
      root_node.expanded = true

      local buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
      vim.bo[buf].buftype = "nofile"
      vim.bo[buf].bufhidden = "wipe"
      vim.bo[buf].filetype = "lsp-hierarchy"
      vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false

      local title = direction == "incoming" and "Incoming Calls" or "Outgoing Calls"
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_name(buf, string.format("[%s] %s()", title, root_node.name))

      local state = { line_map = {}, last_preview = nil }
      local root_nodes = { root_node }

      --- Navigate source_win to a node's call site (or definition fallback).
      local function navigate_to_node(node, focus)
        if not node or not node.uri then return end
        if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then return end

        local nav_pos = get_nav_position(node)
        if not nav_pos then return end

        local target_buf = vim.uri_to_bufnr(node.uri)
        vim.fn.bufload(target_buf)

        if focus then
          vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(source_win)
        end

        vim.api.nvim_win_call(source_win, function()
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(source_win, target_buf)
          local cursor = lsp_pos_to_cursor(target_buf, nav_pos, offset_encoding)
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(source_win, cursor)
          vim.cmd("normal! zz")
        end)
      end

      -- Resolve to configured depth, then display
      resolve_to_depth(client, root_node, direction, source_buf, max_depth, function()
        vim.schedule(function()
          if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) then return end

          refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)

          -- Open in a horizontal split at bottom
          vim.cmd("botright vsplit")
          vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(0, buf)
          vim.cmd("wincmd J")
          vim.cmd("resize 15")
          vim.wo.number = false
          vim.wo.relativenumber = false
          vim.wo.signcolumn = "no"
          vim.wo.cursorline = true
          vim.wo.wrap = false

          -- Store hierarchy window for targeted cursor operations
          state.hier_win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()

          -- Auto-preview: show call site in source window on cursor move
          vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("CursorMoved", {
            buffer = buf,
            callback = function()
              if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then return end
              local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
              local node = state.line_map[lnum]
              if not node or not node.uri or node._loading or node._error then return end

              -- Dedup: skip if same target as last preview
              local nav_pos = get_nav_position(node)
              local preview_key = node.uri .. ":" .. (nav_pos and nav_pos.line or -1)
              if state.last_preview == preview_key then return end
              state.last_preview = preview_key

              pcall(navigate_to_node, node, false)
            end,
          })

          -- Jump to call site (focuses source window)
          local function jump()
            local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
            local node = state.line_map[lnum]
            navigate_to_node(node, true)
          end

          -- Toggle expand/collapse
          local function toggle()
            local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
            local node = state.line_map[lnum]
            if not node or node._loading or node._error then return end

            if node.expanded then
              node.expanded = false
              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
            elseif node._resolved then
              node.expanded = true
              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
            else
              -- Show loading indicator immediately
              node.children = { {
                _loading = true,
                name = "loading...",
                depth = node.depth + 1,
                children = {},
              } }
              node.expanded = true
              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)

              -- Tag this resolve so stale responses are ignored
              node._resolve_gen = (node._resolve_gen or 0) + 1
              local my_gen = node._resolve_gen

              -- Resolve children asynchronously
              resolve_children(client, node, direction, source_buf, function(children, resolve_err)
                vim.schedule(function()
                  if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) then return end
                  if node._resolve_gen ~= my_gen then return end

                  if resolve_err then
                    node.children = { {
                      _error = true,
                      _error_msg = tostring(resolve_err),
                      name = "error",
                      depth = node.depth + 1,
                      children = {},
                    } }
                  else
                    node.children = children or {}
                    for _, child in ipairs(node.children) do
                      child._resolved = false
                    end
                  end
                  node._resolved = true
                  refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
                end)
              end)
            end
          end

          local bopts = { buffer = buf, nowait = true, silent = true }
          vim.keymap.set("n", "<CR>", jump, bopts)
          vim.keymap.set("n", "o", toggle, bopts)
          vim.keymap.set("n", "q", "<cmd>close<cr>", bopts)
          vim.keymap.set("n", "<Esc>", "<cmd>close<cr>", bopts)
        end)
      end)
    end)
  end, source_buf)
end

function M.incoming(opts) M.show("incoming", opts) end
function M.outgoing(opts) M.show("outgoing", opts) end

return M

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Debounce pattern in Neovim**: `vim.uv.new_timer()` + `vim.schedule_wrap` is the canonical approach. The timer fires in the libuv event loop, but `schedule_wrap` ensures the callback runs in Neovim's main loop where API calls are safe. The callback re-reads cursor position after the delay so it previews where you *stopped*, not intermediate positions.
- **Timer lifecycle**: `bufhidden=wipe` means the buffer gets destroyed on window close, so the `BufWipeout` autocmd is the right cleanup hook — `stop()` cancels pending callbacks, `close()` releases the libuv handle.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

message.content: What is the difference between <leader>cI and <leader>cO ?

content.text:
`<leader>cI` shows **incoming calls** — who calls the function under your cursor (callers flowing *in*).

`<leader>cO` shows **outgoing calls** — what the function under your cursor calls (calls flowing *out*).

Both open the same tree viewer; the direction of traversal differs.

From `lua/plugins/lsp.lua:664-665`:
```lua
map("n", "<leader>cI", function() require("lsp-hierarchy").incoming() end, "Incoming Calls Tree")
map("n", "<leader>cO", function() require("lsp-hierarchy").outgoing() end, "Outgoing Calls Tree")
```

There are also lowercase variants (`<leader>ci` / `<leader>co`) that use FzfLua's flat list instead of the recursive tree view.

    35→  [14] = { "󰏿 ", "@constant" },             -- Constant
    36→  [15] = { " ", "String" },                -- String
    37→  [16] = { "󰎠 ", "Number" },                -- Number
    38→  [17] = { "◩ ", "Boolean" },               -- Boolean
    39→  [18] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Array
    40→  [19] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- Object
    41→  [20] = { "󰌋 ", "Identifier" },            -- Key
    42→  [21] = { "󰟢 ", "Comment" },               -- Null
    43→  [22] = { " ", "@lsp.type.enumMember" },  -- EnumMember
    44→  [23] = { "󰙅 ", "Structure" },             -- Struct
    45→  [24] = { " ", "Special" },               -- Event
    46→  [25] = { "󰆕 ", "Operator" },              -- Operator
    47→  [26] = { " ", "Type" },                  -- TypeParameter
    48→}
    49→local KIND_FALLBACK = { "? ", "NonText" }
    50→
    51→local GUIDE_MID    = "├─ "
    52→local GUIDE_LAST   = "└─ "
    53→local GUIDE_NESTED = "│  "
    54→local GUIDE_SPACE  = "   "
    55→
    56→-- ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    57→local function get_short_path(uri)
    58→  local path = vim.uri_to_fname(uri)
    59→  local cwd = vim.fn.getcwd() .. "/"
    60→  if path:sub(1, #cwd) == cwd then
    61→    path = path:sub(#cwd + 1)
    62→  end
    63→  return path
    64→end
    65→
    66→--- Returns the best navigation position for a node: call site (from_ranges)
    67→--- first, falling back to the symbol's selection/definition range.
    68→local function get_nav_position(node)
    69→  if node.from_ranges and node.from_ranges[1] then
    70→    return node.from_ranges[1].start
    71→  end
    72→  if node.range then
    73→    return node.range.start
    74→  end
    75→  return nil
    76→end
    77→
    78→--- Converts an LSP position to a Neovim cursor tuple {1-indexed line, byte col},
    79→--- respecting the client's offset encoding (utf-8/utf-16/utf-32).
    80→local function lsp_pos_to_cursor(target_buf, pos, offset_encoding)
    81→  local row = pos.line + 1
    82→  if pos.character == 0 then
    83→    return { row, 0 }
    84→  end
    85→  -- _get_line_byte_from_position handles encoding conversion internally
    86→  local ok, byte_col = pcall(
    87→    vim.lsp.util._get_line_byte_from_position,
    88→    target_buf, pos, offset_encoding
    89→  )
    90→  if ok then
    91→    return { row, byte_col }
    92→  end
    93→  return { row, pos.character }
    94→end
    95→
    96→local function make_node(item, from_ranges, depth)
    97→  local range = item.selectionRange or item.range
    98→  return {
    99→    name = item.name,
   100→    detail = item.detail or "",
   101→    kind = item.kind,
   102→    uri = item.uri,
   103→    range = range,
   104→    from_ranges = from_ranges,
   105→    children = {},
   106→    expanded = false,
   107→    depth = depth or 0,
   108→    -- Keep the original item for subsequent LSP requests
   109→    _item = item,
   110→  }
   111→end
   112→
   113→-- ── Tree rendering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
   114→
   115→--- Renders the tree into lines with extmark highlight data.
   116→---@param nodes table[]
   117→---@param lines string[]
   118→---@param line_map table[]
   119→---@param extmarks table[][] array of {col_start, col_end, hl_group} per line
   120→---@param last_flags table<integer, boolean> tracks which ancestor depths were last-child
   121→local function render_tree(nodes, lines, line_map, extmarks, last_flags)
   122→  last_flags = last_flags or {}
   123→  lines = lines or {}
   124→  line_map = line_map or {}
   125→  extmarks = extmarks or {}
   126→
   127→  for i, node in ipairs(nodes) do
   128→    local depth = node.depth
   129→    local is_last = (i == #nodes)
   130→    local line_extmarks = {}
   131→    local col = 0
   132→
   133→    -- Build guide prefix for ancestor levels
   134→    local prefix = ""
   135→    for d = 1, depth - 1 do
   136→      local guide = last_flags[d] and GUIDE_SPACE or GUIDE_NESTED
   137→      prefix = prefix .. guide
   138→    end
   139→
   140→    -- Connector (root nodes have none)
   141→    local connector = ""
   142→    if depth > 0 then
   143→      connector = is_last and GUIDE_LAST or GUIDE_MID
   144→    end
   145→
   146→    local guide_str = prefix .. connector
   147→    if #guide_str > 0 then
   148→      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #guide_str, "NonText" })
   149→      col = col + #guide_str
   150→    end
   151→
   152→    local line
   153→
   154→    if node._loading then
   155→      -- Synthetic loading placeholder
   156→      local text = "⟳ loading..."
   157→      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #text, "Comment" })
   158→      line = guide_str .. text
   159→
   160→    elseif node._error then
   161→      -- Synthetic error placeholder
   162→      local text = "✗ " .. (node._error_msg or "error resolving calls")
   163→      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #text, "DiagnosticError" })
   164→      line = guide_str .. text
   165→
   166→    else
   167→      -- Toggle icon
   168→      local toggle_icon
   169→      if #node.children > 0 or not node._resolved then
   170→        toggle_icon = node.expanded and "▼ " or "► "
   171→      else
   172→        toggle_icon = "· "
   173→      end
   174→      local toggle_hl = toggle_icon == "· " and "NonText" or "Special"
   175→      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #toggle_icon, toggle_hl })
   176→      col = col + #toggle_icon
   177→
   178→      -- Kind icon
   179→      local kind_entry = KIND_ICONS[node.kind] or KIND_FALLBACK
   180→      local kind_str = kind_entry[1]
   181→      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #kind_str, kind_entry[2] })
   182→      col = col + #kind_str
   183→
   184→      -- Function name
   185→      local name_str = node.name .. "()"
   186→      table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #name_str, "Function" })
   187→      col = col + #name_str
   188→
   189→      -- Location: show call site line (from_ranges) when available
   190→      local location = ""
   191→      if node.uri then
   192→        local path = get_short_path(node.uri)
   193→        local nav_pos = get_nav_position(node)
   194→        local lnum = nav_pos and (nav_pos.line + 1) or ""
   195→        location = string.format(" [%s:%s]", path, lnum)
   196→        table.insert(line_extmarks, { col, col + #location, "Comment" })
   197→      end
   198→
   199→      line = guide_str .. toggle_icon .. kind_str .. name_str .. location
   200→    end
   201→
   202→    table.insert(lines, line)
   203→    table.insert(line_map, node)
   204→    table.insert(extmarks, line_extmarks)
   205→
   206→    -- Recurse into expanded children
   207→    if node.expanded and #node.children > 0 then
   208→      local old = last_flags[depth]
   209→      last_flags[depth] = is_last
   210→      render_tree(node.children, lines, line_map, extmarks, last_flags)
   211→      last_flags[depth] = old
   212→    end
   213→  end
   214→
   215→  return lines, line_map, extmarks
   216→end
   217→
   218→-- ── Buffer management ────────────────────────────────────────────────
   219→local function refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
   220→  if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) then return end
   221→
   222→  local lines, line_map, ext = render_tree(root_nodes)
   223→  state.line_map = line_map
   224→
   225→  -- Save cursor from the hierarchy window (not window 0)
   226→  local win = state.hier_win
   227→  local cursor = { 1, 0 }
   228→  if win and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(win) then
   229→    local ok, pos = pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor, win)
   230→    if ok then cursor = pos end
   231→  end
   232→
   233→  vim.bo[buf].modifiable = true
   234→  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, lines)
   235→  vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false
   236→
   237→  -- Apply extmark highlights
   238→  vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, ns, 0, -1)
   239→  for line_idx, line_ext in ipairs(ext) do
   240→    for _, e in ipairs(line_ext) do
   241→      pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark, buf, ns, line_idx - 1, e[1], {
   242→        end_col = e[2],
   243→        hl_group = e[3],
   244→      })
   245→    end
   246→  end
   247→
   248→  -- Restore cursor in the hierarchy window only
   249→  local max_line = #lines
   250→  if cursor[1] > max_line then
   251→    cursor[1] = max_line
   252→  end
   253→  if max_line > 0 and win and vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(win) then
   254→    pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, win, cursor)
   255→  end
   256→end
   257→
   258→-- ── LSP resolution ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
   259→local function resolve_children(client, node, direction, bufnr, callback)
   260→  local method = direction == "incoming"
   261→    and "callHierarchy/incomingCalls"
   262→    or "callHierarchy/outgoingCalls"
   263→
   264→  local item = node._item
   265→  client:request(method, { item = item }, function(err, result)
   266→    if err then
   267→      callback(nil, err)
   268→      return
   269→    end
   270→    if not result then
   271→      callback({})
   272→      return
   273→    end
   274→
   275→    local children = {}
   276→    for _, call in ipairs(result) do
   277→      local source = direction == "incoming" and call.from or call.to
   278→      local from_ranges = call.fromRanges
   279→      local child = make_node(source, from_ranges, node.depth + 1)
   280→      table.insert(children, child)
   281→    end
   282→    callback(children)
   283→  end, bufnr)
   284→end
   285→
   286→--- Recursively resolves children up to max_depth levels using async fan-out.
   287→local function resolve_to_depth(client, node, direction, bufnr, max_depth, callback)
   288→  if node.depth >= max_depth then
   289→    callback()
   290→    return
   291→  end
   292→
   293→  resolve_children(client, node, direction, bufnr, function(children, err)
   294→    if err or not children then
   295→      node.children = {}
   296→      node._resolved = true
   297→      callback()
   298→      return
   299→    end
   300→
   301→    node.children = children
   302→    node._resolved = true
   303→    node.expanded = true
   304→
   305→    -- Count children that need further resolution
   306→    local pending = 0
   307→    for _, child in ipairs(children) do
   308→      child._resolved = false
   309→      if node.depth + 1 < max_depth then
   310→        pending = pending + 1
   311→      end
   312→    end
   313→
   314→    if pending == 0 then
   315→      callback()
   316→      return
   317→    end
   318→
   319→    local completed = 0
   320→    for _, child in ipairs(children) do
   321→      if node.depth + 1 < max_depth then
   322→        resolve_to_depth(client, child, direction, bufnr, max_depth, function()
   323→          completed = completed + 1
   324→          if completed == pending then
   325→            callback()
   326→          end
   327→        end)
   328→      end
   329→    end
   330→  end)
   331→end
   332→
   333→-- ── Main entry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   334→function M.show(direction, opts)
   335→  direction = direction or "incoming"
   336→  opts = opts or {}
   337→  local max_depth = opts.depth or 2
   338→
   339→  local source_buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
   340→  local source_win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
   341→  local params = vim.lsp.util.make_position_params(0, "utf-16")
   342→
   343→  local clients = vim.lsp.get_clients({
   344→    bufnr = source_buf,
   345→    method = "textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy",
   346→  })
   347→
   348→  if #clients == 0 then
   349→    vim.notify("No LSP client supports call hierarchy", vim.log.levels.WARN)
   350→    return
   351→  end
   352→
   353→  local client = clients[1]
   354→  local offset_encoding = client.offset_encoding or "utf-16"
   355→
   356→  client:request("textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy", params, function(err, result)
   357→    if err or not result or #result == 0 then
   358→      vim.notify("No call hierarchy item found at cursor", vim.log.levels.WARN)
   359→      return
   360→    end
   361→
   362→    vim.schedule(function()
   363→      local root_item = result[1]
   364→      local root_node = make_node(root_item, nil, 0)
   365→      root_node.expanded = true
   366→
   367→      local buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
   368→      vim.bo[buf].buftype = "nofile"
   369→      vim.bo[buf].bufhidden = "wipe"
   370→      vim.bo[buf].filetype = "lsp-hierarchy"
   371→      vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false
   372→
   373→      local title = direction == "incoming" and "Incoming Calls" or "Outgoing Calls"
   374→      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_name(buf, string.format("[%s] %s()", title, root_node.name))
   375→
   376→      local state = { line_map = {}, last_preview = nil }
   377→      local root_nodes = { root_node }
   378→
   379→      --- Navigate source_win to a node's call site (or definition fallback).
   380→      local function navigate_to_node(node, focus)
   381→        if not node or not node.uri then return end
   382→        if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then return end
   383→
   384→        local nav_pos = get_nav_position(node)
   385→        if not nav_pos then return end
   386→
   387→        local target_buf = vim.uri_to_bufnr(node.uri)
   388→        vim.fn.bufload(target_buf)
   389→
   390→        if focus then
   391→          vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(source_win)
   392→        end
   393→
   394→        vim.api.nvim_win_call(source_win, function()
   395→          vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(source_win, target_buf)
   396→          local cursor = lsp_pos_to_cursor(target_buf, nav_pos, offset_encoding)
   397→          vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(source_win, cursor)
   398→          vim.cmd("normal! zz")
   399→        end)
   400→      end
   401→
   402→      -- Resolve to configured depth, then display
   403→      resolve_to_depth(client, root_node, direction, source_buf, max_depth, function()
   404→        vim.schedule(function()
   405→          if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) then return end
   406→
   407→          refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
   408→
   409→          -- Open in a horizontal split at bottom
   410→          vim.cmd("botright vsplit")
   411→          vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(0, buf)
   412→          vim.cmd("wincmd J")
   413→          vim.cmd("resize 15")
   414→          vim.wo.number = false
   415→          vim.wo.relativenumber = false
   416→          vim.wo.signcolumn = "no"
   417→          vim.wo.cursorline = true
   418→          vim.wo.wrap = false
   419→
   420→          -- Store hierarchy window for targeted cursor operations
   421→          state.hier_win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
   422→
   423→          -- Auto-preview: show call site in source window on cursor move.
   424→          -- Debounced (30ms) so holding j/k doesn't thrash the source window.
   425→          local preview_timer = vim.uv.new_timer()
   426→
   427→          vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufWipeout", {
   428→            buffer = buf,
   429→            once = true,
   430→            callback = function()
   431→              preview_timer:stop()
   432→              preview_timer:close()
   433→            end,
   434→          })
   435→
   436→          vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("CursorMoved", {
   437→            buffer = buf,
   438→            callback = function()
   439→              preview_timer:stop()
   440→              if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then return end
   441→
   442→              preview_timer:start(30, 0, vim.schedule_wrap(function()
   443→                if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) then return end
   444→                if not vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then return end
   445→
   446→                local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
   447→                local node = state.line_map[lnum]
   448→                if not node or not node.uri or node._loading or node._error then return end
   449→
   450→                -- Dedup: skip if exact same target (uri + line + character)
   451→                local nav_pos = get_nav_position(node)
   452→                local preview_key = node.uri
   453→                  .. ":" .. (nav_pos and nav_pos.line or -1)
   454→                  .. ":" .. (nav_pos and nav_pos.character or -1)
   455→                if state.last_preview == preview_key then return end
   456→                state.last_preview = preview_key
   457→
   458→                pcall(navigate_to_node, node, false)
   459→              end))
   460→            end,
   461→          })
   462→
   463→          -- Jump to call site (focuses source window)
   464→          local function jump()
   465→            local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
   466→            local node = state.line_map[lnum]
   467→            navigate_to_node(node, true)
   468→          end
   469→
   470→          -- Toggle expand/collapse
   471→          local function toggle()
   472→            local lnum = vim.fn.line(".")
   473→            local node = state.line_map[lnum]
   474→            if not node or node._loading or node._error then return end
   475→
   476→            if node.expanded then
   477→              node.expanded = false
   478→              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
   479→            elseif node._resolved then
   480→              node.expanded = true
   481→              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
   482→            else
   483→              -- Show loading indicator immediately
   484→              node.children = { {
   485→                _loading = true,
   486→                name = "loading...",
   487→                depth = node.depth + 1,
   488→                children = {},
   489→              } }
   490→              node.expanded = true
   491→              refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
   492→
   493→              -- Tag this resolve so stale responses are ignored
   494→              node._resolve_gen = (node._resolve_gen or 0) + 1
   495→              local my_gen = node._resolve_gen
   496→
   497→              -- Resolve children asynchronously
   498→              resolve_children(client, node, direction, source_buf, function(children, resolve_err)
   499→                vim.schedule(function()
   500→                  if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf) then return end
   501→                  if node._resolve_gen ~= my_gen then return end
   502→
   503→                  if resolve_err then
   504→                    node.children = { {
   505→                      _error = true,
   506→                      _error_msg = tostring(resolve_err),
   507→                      name = "error",
   508→                      depth = node.depth + 1,
   509→                      children = {},
   510→                    } }
   511→                  else
   512→                    node.children = children or {}
   513→                    for _, child in ipairs(node.children) do
   514→                      child._resolved = false
   515→                    end
   516→                  end
   517→                  node._resolved = true
   518→                  refresh_buffer(buf, root_nodes, state)
   519→                end)
   520→              end)
   521→            end
   522→          end
   523→
   524→          local bopts = { buffer = buf, nowait = true, silent = true }
   525→          vim.keymap.set("n", "<CR>", jump, bopts)
   526→          vim.keymap.set("n", "o", toggle, bopts)
   527→          vim.keymap.set("n", "q", "<cmd>close<cr>", bopts)
   528→          vim.keymap.set("n", "<Esc>", "<cmd>close<cr>", bopts)
   529→        end)
   530→      end)
   531→    end)
   532→  end, source_buf)
   533→end
   534→
   535→function M.incoming(opts) M.show("incoming", opts) end
   536→function M.outgoing(opts) M.show("outgoing", opts) end
   537→
   538→return M

1→-- Basic Neovim Options
     2→-- Core editor settings for nvim-mini
     3→
     4→local opt = vim.opt
     5→
     6→-- Line numbers
     7→opt.number = true
     8→opt.relativenumber = true
     9→
    10→-- Statuscolumn: signs + right-aligned hybrid line number
    11→-- %l = "line number column for currently drawn line" (:help statuscolumn).
    12→-- With nu+rnu, the number column shows hybrid (:help number_relativenumber):
    13→-- absolute on cursor line, relative elsewhere — and %l mirrors that exactly.
    14→-- Verified on 0.11.5: cursor@10 → lnum 9→"1", 10→"10", 11→"1" (hybrid).
    15→-- Previously "%s %{v:lnum} %{v:relnum}" (both numbers side-by-side) but %{}
    16→-- expressions evaluate Vimscript per visible line per redraw causing scroll stutter.
    17→opt.statuscolumn = "%s%=%l "
    18→
    19→-- Clipboard - Custom OSC-52 with explicit tmux passthrough
    20→-- The built-in vim.ui.clipboard.osc52 doesn't wrap sequences for tmux correctly.
    21→-- Disable with: vim.g.clipboard_disable_osc52 = true (before this file loads)
    22→
    23→-- Detect whether the terminal likely supports OSC 52
    24→local function osc52_supported()
    25→  if vim.g.clipboard_disable_osc52 then return false end
    26→  -- Known-good: tmux, screen, xterm-family, ghostty, wezterm, alacritty, kitty
    27→  local term = vim.env.TERM or ""
    28→  if vim.env.TMUX or vim.env.SSH_TTY or vim.env.KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST or vim.env.DEVCONTAINER then
    29→    return true -- remote contexts always need OSC52 for clipboard
    30→  end
    31→  return term:match("xterm") or term:match("screen") or term:match("tmux")
    32→    or term:match("ghostty") or term:match("wezterm") or term:match("alacritty")
    33→    or term:match("kitty") or vim.env.TERM_PROGRAM ~= nil
    34→end
    35→
    36→if osc52_supported() then
    37→  local function osc52_copy(lines, regtype)
    38→    local text = table.concat(lines, "\n")
    39→    local encoded = vim.base64.encode(text)
    40→    local osc = string.format("\027]52;c;%s\a", encoded)
    41→
    42→    -- Wrap for tmux passthrough if:
    43→    -- 1. In tmux directly ($TMUX set)
    44→    -- 2. In SSH session (likely through tmux on local machine)
    45→    -- 3. In Kubernetes container (kubectl exec/debug through tmux)
    46→    -- 4. In devcontainer (docker exec through tmux)
    47→    local needs_tmux_wrap = vim.env.TMUX
    48→      or vim.env.SSH_TTY
    49→      or vim.env.KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
    50→      or vim.env.DEVCONTAINER
    51→
    52→    if needs_tmux_wrap then
    53→      osc = string.format("\027Ptmux;\027%s\027\\", osc)
    54→    end

   149→  -- Get line numbers

   186→-- Build a GitHub permalink for current file + lines
   187→local function github_permalink(opts)

You're right — let me give my actual recommendation with reasoning instead of deflecting.

**Yes, auto-folding the source window during hierarchy preview would be valuable.** Here's my reasoning:

**Why it helps**: The hierarchy viewer's whole purpose is focused call-chain exploration. Showing the full unfolded source file is noise — you only care about the call site and its surrounding function context. The preview already changes the buffer and moves the cursor; folding is a natural extension of that focus.

**How it should work**: Always on during preview. If you wanted the full file, you'd navigate there directly (`<CR>`), not browse the tree. The implementation is a single Neovim command — `zMzv` (fold all, reveal just the enclosing scope around cursor) — which works natively with the existing treesitter+ufo folding.

**Fold restoration**: The config defaults to `foldlevel = 99` (all folds open). On hierarchy close, restore that default. This is safe because treesitter folds are deterministic — `foldlevel = 99` always produces the same "all open" result.

# Auto-fold source window during hierarchy preview

## Context

The LSP call hierarchy tree viewer (`<leader>cI`/`<leader>cO`) previews call sites
in the source window as you navigate. Currently the source window shows the full
unfolded file — this is noisy when the goal is focused call-chain exploration.
Adding `zMzv` to the preview collapses all folds then reveals just the enclosing
function around the call site, removing irrelevant code from view.

## File to modify

- `~/neovim-hierarchy/lua/lsp-hierarchy.lua`

## Changes

### 1. Add `zMzv` to navigate_to_node (~line 395)

Inside the `nvim_win_call(source_win, ...)` block, after `vim.cmd("normal! zz")`:

```lua
vim.cmd("normal! zMzv")
```

This folds everything (`zM`) then opens just the folds containing the cursor line
(`zv`). Works natively with nvim-ufo + treesitter folding already configured.

### 2. Restore folds on hierarchy close

In the `BufWipeout` autocmd that already exists for the preview timer cleanup
(~line 430), also restore the source window's fold state:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufWipeout", {
  buffer = buf,
  once = true,
  callback = function()
    preview_timer:stop()
    preview_timer:close()
    -- Restore folds: config default is foldlevel=99 (all open)
    if vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then
      vim.wo[source_win].foldlevel = 99
    end
  end,
})
```

`foldlevel = 99` is the configured default (set in lsp-enhancements.lua:46).
Treesitter folds are deterministic, so this reliably restores "all open".

## Why this is safe

- `zM`/`zv` are compatible with nvim-ufo (built on top of native fold infra)
- View persistence (`mkview`/`loadview` in lsp-enhancements.lua:50-77) saves on
  `BufWinLeave` — the pre-hierarchy fold state is saved before hierarchy opens,
  and `foldlevel = 99` on close prevents stale folded state from persisting
- No new dependencies, no new keymaps, no config changes needed

## Verification

1. Open a Go/TS file with multiple functions
2. `<leader>cI` on a function — hierarchy opens, source folds to just the root function
3. `j`/`k` through the tree — source window folds/unfolds to show each call site's enclosing function
4. `q` to close hierarchy — source window folds restore to all-open
5. Confirm existing fold state (manual folds, ufo virtual text) works normally after close

# Auto-fold source window during hierarchy preview

## Context

The LSP call hierarchy tree viewer (`<leader>cI`/`<leader>cO`) previews call sites
in the source window as you navigate. Currently the source window shows the full
unfolded file — this is noisy when the goal is focused call-chain exploration.
Adding `zMzv` to the preview collapses all folds then reveals just the enclosing
function around the call site, removing irrelevant code from view.

## File to modify

- `~/neovim-hierarchy/lua/lsp-hierarchy.lua`

## Changes

### 1. Add `zMzv` to navigate_to_node (~line 395)

Inside the `nvim_win_call(source_win, ...)` block, after `vim.cmd("normal! zz")`:

```lua
vim.cmd("normal! zMzv")
```

This folds everything (`zM`) then opens just the folds containing the cursor line
(`zv`). Works natively with nvim-ufo + treesitter folding already configured.

### 2. Restore folds on hierarchy close

In the `BufWipeout` autocmd that already exists for the preview timer cleanup
(~line 430), also restore the source window's fold state:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufWipeout", {
  buffer = buf,
  once = true,
  callback = function()
    preview_timer:stop()
    preview_timer:close()
    -- Restore folds: config default is foldlevel=99 (all open)
    if vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then
      vim.wo[source_win].foldlevel = 99
    end
  end,
})
```

`foldlevel = 99` is the configured default (set in lsp-enhancements.lua:46).
Treesitter folds are deterministic, so this reliably restores "all open".

## Why this is safe

- `zM`/`zv` are compatible with nvim-ufo (built on top of native fold infra)
- View persistence (`mkview`/`loadview` in lsp-enhancements.lua:50-77) saves on
  `BufWinLeave` — the pre-hierarchy fold state is saved before hierarchy opens,
  and `foldlevel = 99` on close prevents stale folded state from persisting
- No new dependencies, no new keymaps, no config changes needed

## Verification

1. Open a Go/TS file with multiple functions
2. `<leader>cI` on a function — hierarchy opens, source folds to just the root function
3. `j`/`k` through the tree — source window folds/unfolds to show each call site's enclosing function
4. `q` to close hierarchy — source window folds restore to all-open
5. Confirm existing fold state (manual folds, ufo virtual text) works normally after close

## Context

The LSP call hierarchy tree viewer (`<leader>cI`/`<leader>cO`) previews call sites
in the source window as you navigate the tree. Currently the source window shows
the full unfolded file — noisy when exploring call chains. Adding `zMzv` to the
preview folds everything then reveals just the enclosing function around the call
site, making hierarchy exploration a focused experience rather than a cursor-chasing one.

## File to modify

- `lua/lsp-hierarchy.lua`

## Changes

### 1. Auto-fold on preview (navigate_to_node, ~line 395)

Inside the `nvim_win_call(source_win, ...)` block, after `vim.cmd("normal! zz")`,
add fold-focus:

```lua
vim.cmd("normal! zMzv")
```

`zM` folds everything, `zv` opens just the folds enclosing the cursor line —
typically the function body containing the call site. Works natively with the
existing nvim-ufo + treesitter fold setup.

### 2. No fold on `<CR>` jump

The `jump` function calls `navigate_to_node(node, true)` which focuses the source
window. Since `<CR>` means "I'm done browsing, take me there", it should **not**
fold — the user is transitioning to free exploration. Split `navigate_to_node` to
accept a `fold` flag:

```lua
local function navigate_to_node(node, focus, fold)
  ...
  vim.api.nvim_win_call(source_win, function()
    ...
    vim.cmd("normal! zz")
    if fold then
      vim.cmd("normal! zMzv")
    end
  end)
end
```

- CursorMoved preview calls: `navigate_to_node(node, false, true)` — fold
- `<CR>` jump calls: `navigate_to_node(node, true, false)` — no fold

Extend the existing `BufWipeout` autocmd (preview timer cleanup, ~line 430) to
also restore fold state:

```lua

  buffer = buf,

  callback = function()
    preview_timer:stop()
    preview_timer:close()
    if vim.api.nvim_win_is_valid(source_win) then
      vim.wo[source_win].foldlevel = 99
    end
  end,
})
```

folds are deterministic, so this reliably restores the "all open" baseline.

## Why this is safe

- `zM`/`zv` are compatible with nvim-ufo (built on Neovim's native fold infra)
- View persistence (`mkview`/`loadview` in lsp-enhancements.lua:50-77) saves on
  `BufWinLeave` — pre-hierarchy state is saved before hierarchy opens, and
  `foldlevel = 99` on close prevents stale folded state from persisting
- No new dependencies, keymaps, or config changes

## Verification

1. Open a Go/TS file with multiple functions
2. `<leader>cI` on a function — hierarchy opens, source folds to enclosing function
3. `j`/`k` through tree — source re-folds to each call site's enclosing function
4. `<CR>` to jump — source window unfolds (no fold-focus), cursor in source window
5. Re-open hierarchy, `q` to close — folds restore to all-open
6. Confirm ufo virtual text ("... N lines") renders correctly on folded lines

[Image: source: /var/folders/5p/gmrrr9ws5g98h04tn8scp6s40000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_OHRr9T/Screenshot 2026-03-22 at 19.11.09.png]

I can see the issue. The hierarchy tree is too monotone — guides, locations, and leaf icons all share the same grey (`NonText`/`Comment`), making the tree feel washed out against the Tokyo Night background.

Let me explore what highlight groups would work better, then update the plan.

     3→-- Clipboard diff utilities
     4→local function compare_clipboard()
     5→	-- Get clipboard content
     6→	local clipboard = vim.fn.getreg("+")
     7→	if clipboard == "" then
     8→		vim.notify("Clipboard is empty", vim.log.levels.WARN)
     9→		return
    10→	end
    11→
    12→	-- Store current filetype and buffer for syntax highlighting
    13→	local ft = vim.bo.filetype
    14→	local original_buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
    15→
    16→	-- Create vertical split with clipboard content
    17→	vim.cmd("vnew")
    18→	local scratch_buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
    19→	vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(scratch_buf, 0, -1, false, vim.split(clipboard, "\n"))
    20→	vim.bo[scratch_buf].buftype = "nofile"
    21→	vim.bo[scratch_buf].bufhidden = "wipe"
    22→	vim.bo[scratch_buf].filetype = ft
    23→	vim.cmd("diffthis")
    24→
    25→	-- Function to close the diff (works from either buffer)
    26→	local function close_diff()
    27→		vim.cmd("diffoff!")
    28→		-- Close scratch buffer if it exists
    29→		if vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(scratch_buf) then
    30→			vim.cmd("bwipeout " .. scratch_buf)
    31→		end
    32→	end
    33→
    34→	-- Add q to close the diff on BOTH buffers
    35→	vim.keymap.set("n", "q", close_diff, { buffer = scratch_buf, desc = "Close diff" })
    36→	vim.keymap.set("n", "q", close_diff, { buffer = original_buf, desc = "Close diff" })
    37→
    38→	-- Go back to original window and enable diff
    39→	vim.cmd("wincmd p")
    40→	vim.cmd("diffthis")
    41→end

    43→local function compare_clipboard_selection()
    44→	-- Exit visual mode to set the '< and '> marks
    45→	vim.cmd('normal! "vy') -- Also yanks selection to register v as backup
    46→
    47→	-- Get clipboard content

    49→	if clipboard == "" then
    50→		vim.notify("Clipboard is empty", vim.log.levels.WARN)

    52→	end

    54→	-- Get visual selection using the now-set marks

    56→	local end_pos = vim.fn.getpos("'>")
    57→	local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, start_pos[2] - 1, end_pos[2], false)

    59→	if #lines == 0 then

    64→	-- Store current filetype

    67→	-- Create new tab with two splits

    76→	vim.cmd("vnew")

   132→-- Find the repo/worktree root by walking up from dir to find .git.
   133→-- Returns the directory containing .git (the working tree root), or nil.
   134→-- Uses fs_stat only (no subprocess).
   135→local function find_repo_root(dir)
   136→	local d = dir
   137→	while d and d ~= "" and d ~= "/" do
   138→		if vim.uv.fs_stat(d .. "/.git") then
   139→			return d
   140→		end
   141→		local parent = vim.fn.fnamemodify(d, ":h")
   142→		if parent == d then
   143→			break
   144→		end
   145→		d = parent
   146→	end
   147→	return nil
   148→end

   150→-- Check if `path` is equal to or under `root` (path-separator-aware).
   151→-- Avoids false positives like "/dotfiles" matching "/dotfiles-mergeview".
   152→local function path_is_under(path, root)
   153→	if not root or not path then
   154→		return false
   155→	end
   156→	return path == root or path:sub(1, #root + 1) == root .. "/"
   157→end

   159→-- Get the working directory of the current terminal buffer's shell process.
   160→-- On macOS: queries lsof for the process cwd. On Linux: reads /proc/PID/cwd.
   161→-- Returns nil if not in a terminal buffer or if detection fails.
   162→local function get_terminal_cwd()
   163→	local job_id = vim.b.terminal_job_id
   164→	if not job_id then
   165→		return nil
   166→	end
   167→	local ok, pid = pcall(vim.fn.jobpid, job_id)
   168→	if not ok or not pid or pid <= 0 then
   169→		return nil
   170→	end
   171→	local cwd = nil
   172→	if vim.fn.has("mac") == 1 then
   173→		local out = vim.fn.system("lsof -nP -a -p " .. pid .. " -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null")
   174→		-- lsof output: "p<pid>\nn<cwd>\n" — extract the n-prefixed line
   175→		cwd = out:match("\nn(.-)\n") or out:match("\nn(.+)$")
   176→	else
   177→		local out = vim.fn.system("readlink /proc/" .. pid .. "/cwd 2>/dev/null")
   178→		if vim.v.shell_error == 0 then
   179→			cwd = out:gsub("\n$", "")
   180→		end
   181→	end
   182→	if cwd and cwd ~= "" then
   183→		return cwd
   184→	end
   185→	return nil
   186→end

   188→-- Resolve the tmux window ID containing Neovim's pane ($TMUX_PANE).

   190→-- bleed when multiple clients or windows are attached to the same session.
   191→-- PERF: Cached for session lifetime — window ID never changes for a Neovim instance.
   192→local _cached_window_id = nil
   193→local function get_neovim_window_id()
   194→	if _cached_window_id then
   195→		return _cached_window_id
   196→	end
   197→	if not vim.env.TMUX or not vim.env.TMUX_PANE then

   200→	local out = vim.fn.system(
   201→		"tmux display-message -p -t " .. vim.fn.shellescape(vim.env.TMUX_PANE) .. " '#{window_id}' 2>/dev/null"
   202→	)

   204→		return nil
   205→	end
   206→	local wid = out:gsub("\n$", "")
   207→	if wid == "" then
   208→		return nil
   209→	end

   211→	return wid
   212→end

   214→-- Get the cwd of the last-selected pane in Neovim's window.
   215→-- Scoped via window ID derived from $TMUX_PANE (not global {last}).
   216→-- Best for FocusGained: when Neovim just gained focus, {last} within its
   217→-- window = the shell pane the user was just in.

   219→	local wid = get_neovim_window_id()

   221→		return nil
   222→	end
   223→	-- Target: <window_id>.{last} — the previously selected pane in this window.
   224→	local target = wid .. ".{last}"
   225→	local out = vim.fn.system(
   226→		"tmux display-message -p -t " .. vim.fn.shellescape(target) .. " '#{pane_current_path}' 2>/dev/null"
   227→	)
   228→	if vim.v.shell_error ~= 0 then
   229→		return nil
   230→	end
   231→	local path = out:gsub("\n$", "")
   232→	if path == "" then
   233→		return nil
   234→	end

   238→-- Async version of get_tmux_last_pane_cwd: non-blocking tmux IPC.
   239→-- Calls callback(cwd_or_nil) when complete.
   240→local function get_tmux_last_pane_cwd_async(callback)
   241→	local wid = get_neovim_window_id()
   242→	if not wid then
   243→		callback(nil)
   244→		return
   245→	end
   246→	local target = wid .. ".{last}"
   247→	vim.system(
   248→		{ "tmux", "display-message", "-p", "-t", target, "#{pane_current_path}" },
   249→		{ text = true },
   250→		function(result)
   251→			vim.schedule(function()
   252→				if result.code ~= 0 or not result.stdout then
   253→					callback(nil)
   254→					return
   255→				end
   256→				local path = result.stdout:gsub("\n$", "")
   257→				callback(path ~= "" and path or nil)
   258→			end)
   259→		end
   260→	)
   261→end

   263→-- Get the cwd of the currently active (focused) pane in Neovim's window,
   264→-- skipping if it's Neovim's own pane. Scoped to Neovim's window via -t.
   265→-- Best for timer polling: when the user is in a shell pane, the active pane
   266→-- in Neovim's window is the shell (correct). {last} would return Neovim's
   267→-- own pane (wrong), causing the timer to override Fish hook results.
   268→local function get_tmux_active_pane_cwd()
   269→	local wid = get_neovim_window_id()
   270→	if not wid then
   271→		return nil
   272→	end
   273→	local out = vim.fn.system(
   274→		"tmux list-panes -t " .. vim.fn.shellescape(wid)
   275→			.. " -F '#{pane_active} #{pane_id} #{pane_current_path}' 2>/dev/null"
   276→	)
   277→	if vim.v.shell_error ~= 0 then
   278→		return nil
   279→	end
   280→	for line in out:gmatch("[^\n]+") do
   281→		local active, pane_id, path = line:match("^(%d) (%%%d+) (.+)$")
   282→		if active == "1" then
   283→			-- Skip if the active pane is Neovim's own pane
   284→			if pane_id == vim.env.TMUX_PANE then
   285→				return nil
   286→			end
   287→			if path == "" then
   288→				return nil
   289→			end
   290→			return path
   291→		end
   292→	end
   293→	return nil
   294→end

   296→-- Async version of get_tmux_active_pane_cwd: non-blocking tmux IPC.
   297→-- PERF: This is the hot path — called every timer tick. Using vim.system()
   298→-- prevents blocking Neovim's UI thread, which is critical when multiple
   299→-- Neovim instances all poll tmux's single-threaded server simultaneously.
   300→-- Calls callback(cwd_or_nil) when complete.
   301→local function get_tmux_active_pane_cwd_async(callback)
   302→	local wid = get_neovim_window_id()
   303→	if not wid then
   304→		callback(nil)
   305→		return
   306→	end
   307→	vim.system(
   308→		{ "tmux", "list-panes", "-t", wid, "-F", "#{pane_active} #{pane_id} #{pane_current_path}" },
   309→		{ text = true },
   310→		function(result)
   311→			vim.schedule(function()
   312→				if result.code ~= 0 or not result.stdout then
   313→					callback(nil)
   314→					return
   315→				end
   316→				for line in result.stdout:gmatch("[^\n]+") do
   317→					local active, pane_id, path = line:match("^(%d) (%%%d+) (.+)$")
   318→					if active == "1" then
   319→						if pane_id == vim.env.TMUX_PANE or path == "" then
   320→							callback(nil)
   321→							return
   322→						end
   323→						callback(path)
   324→						return
   325→					end
   326→				end
   327→				callback(nil)
   328→			end)
   329→		end
   330→	)
   331→end
